questions: Did s-bend off-track exits fall below 4 of 20 at wheel_track 0.16, compared with 4 at 0.14?
Did s-bend max_error stay at or below 0.034, or did the wider track make bends sluggish?
Did steering_oscillation stay below about 0.4 on the oval and s-bend, and did the oval finish stay at 1.0?
Did slalom line_loss_events change from about 1.05 at wheel_track 0.14, or is slalom still 0 of 20?
Is kp 4.0 still adequate at 0.16, or does the wider track now need kp raised to hold the line on bends?

intent: Change one variable from the best design (iteration 7, wheel_track 0.14, score 628.6): raise wheel_track to 0.16 m, keeping sensors at y 0.08 with 16 mm footprints and the ±0.024 m span, and keeping body, wheels and mass unchanged. This continues the monotone track-width trend (0.10 → 496.4, 0.12 → 561.6, 0.14 → 628.6). Expected: s-bend off-track exits fall below 4 of 20, s-bend control_effort falls below 8.9, oval finish stays at 1.0, and steering_oscillation stays below about 0.4. If max_error rises above 0.034 or s-bend exits rise above 4, revert to wheel_track 0.14 as the baseline.
learning: Iteration 7 (wheel_track 0.14) confirmed that the narrower-track direction was wrong at y 0.08: track width 0.10 → 0.12 → 0.14 improved the score monotonically (496.4, 561.6, 628.6), with s-bend off-track exits falling from 15 to 9 to 4. The earlier theory that a wider track reduces steering authority did not hold, so trust the race data over the contract-derived reasoning. Slalom is still 0 of 20 at every geometry tested, so after track width is settled, the next step for slalom needs its own test rather than more lookahead or span changes.
rationale: Iteration 7 (wheel_track 0.14, sensor y 0.08, 16 mm footprints, x ±0.024) is the best design so far at 628.6. Its s-bend finished 16 of 20 (4 off-track exits, down from 9 at wheel_track 0.12 and 15 at 0.10), max_error fell to 0.034, and control_effort fell to 8.9 from 12.2. The oval stayed at 20 of 20 with oscillation 0.19, and s-bend oscillation was 0.32, under the 0.4 gate. Track width now has a monotone gradient at y 0.08: 0.10 gives 496.4, 0.12 gives 561.6 and 0.14 gives 628.6. Integrator feedback (R1) gave the condition for the next step (s-bend exits fell, oscillation below 0.4, oval at 1.0), and all of it is met, so I am following its first requested change and moving to wheel_track 0.16. I am also setting aside the earlier claim that a wider track reduces steering authority. The race data contradicts that theory, so I am using the measured trend. The rest of the geometry stays fixed, with sensors at y 0.08, the 0.024 m span and 16 mm footprints, so the result isolates track width. Expected: s-bend off-track exits fall below 4 of 20 and control_effort falls further, with the oval still at 1.0. Risk: a wider track may make bends sluggish. If max_error rises above 0.034 or s-bend off-track exits rise above 4, revert to wheel_track 0.14 (the iteration 7 design). Slalom has stayed 0 of 20 at every geometry tested, so it is not the target of this step.
